title: Practice: Single and Double Replacement Reactions
description: Low-stakes practice on identifying single replacement and double replacement reaction patterns.

questions.question: Which general pattern represents a single replacement reaction?
questions.explanation: Single replacement has one free element replacing one part of a compound: A + BC -> AC + B.

questions.question: Which general pattern represents a double replacement reaction?
questions.explanation: Double replacement happens when two compounds exchange partners, matching AB + CD -> AD + CB.

questions.question: Classify the reaction: Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu
questions.explanation: Fe is a free element that replaces Cu in CuSO4, so the reaction is single replacement.

questions.question: Classify the reaction: AgNO3 + NaCl -> AgCl + NaNO3
questions.explanation: Both reactants are compounds, and their partners switch: Ag pairs with Cl, while Na pairs with NO3.

questions.question: True or False: In a single replacement reaction, one free element replaces another element in a compound.
questions.explanation: True. That is the core idea of the single replacement pattern A + BC -> AC + B.

questions.question: True or False: A reaction with two products must always be a double replacement reaction.
questions.explanation: False. Single replacement reactions also often have two products. You must track the partner changes.

questions.question: Fill in the reaction type: Zn + 2HCl -> ZnCl2 + H2 is a _____ replacement reaction.
questions.explanation: Zn is a free element that replaces hydrogen in HCl, so it is a single replacement reaction.

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain why BaCl2 + Na2SO4 -> BaSO4 + 2NaCl is a double replacement reaction.
questions.correctAnswer: It is double replacement because two compounds exchange partners. Ba pairs with SO4, and Na pairs with Cl.
questions.explanation: The key evidence is that both reactants are compounds and the positive and negative parts switch partners.
